Updated guidance issued overnight will refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.

Persistent cloud cover and evaporative cooling from rain suppress surface heating, pulling realized highs several degrees below the clear-sky potential. Historical August climatology for Busan (average daily maximum ~29–30 °C) supports this range, while sea-breeze moderation from the Korea Strait adds further restraint.  

The tight clustering around 28 °C (37.5 % market-implied probability) reflects traders’ assessment that partial clearing or delayed convective onset could briefly allow warming to the upper 20s, whereas stronger or earlier rainfall would cap the day at 27 °C or below. Higher outcomes (30 °C+) carry low probability because the current moisture-laden airmass and model consensus favor continued instability through the 17th. Updated KMA briefings and any shifts in precipitation timing remain the key near-term catalysts that could move these implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent KMA and model guidance point to a maximum of 30–33°C at the Incheon International Airport station on August 18, 2026, positioning 29–31°C as the leading market outcomes.** 

August remains within South Korea’s climatological peak warmth, but mid-month patterns show a transition from earlier monsoon-driven rains and cloud cover (which capped August 16 near 27°C) toward building high pressure and reduced precipitation chances. Official short-range forecasts indicate mostly clear morning conditions giving way to increasing afternoon cloudiness, with sea-breeze effects and modest humidity potentially limiting the exact peak at the coastal Incheon site. Ensemble consensus and recent runs cluster daytime highs around 30–32°C, aligning with the 35.5% implied probability on 30°C and comparable shares on 29°C and 31°C. 

Traders appear to be weighting the narrow spread of reliable model outputs and historical August variability at the station, where small shifts in timing of cloud build-up or wind direction can swing the daily maximum by 1–2°C. Upcoming KMA updates and refined model runs over the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities further.

Official forecasts from the India Meteorological Department and models highlight thundery showers and overcast skies expected to limit daytime solar heating, keeping highs near or slightly below the seasonal average of about 32 °C. Persistent moisture and possible localized heavy rain further suppress peak temperatures by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing insolation. Traders appear to weigh these near-term convective patterns against any brief clearing that could allow brief warming to 32–33 °C. Updated model runs and IMD briefings over the next 48 hours will likely refine the range.
